name: Portland Head Light, Fort Williams Park
highlight: The 1791 tower stands on a bare shelf of rock with the surf breaking below it and Ram Island Ledge Light out on the water. Cliffside Plaza, a few hundred feet north, looks straight down the shoreline at the light.

fact.verbatim: Ceremonies of twenty or more people require a permit. If you have fewer than 20, a permit is the only way to reserve a location.

permit.authority: Town of Cape Elizabeth — Cape Elizabeth Community Services / Fort Williams Park

crowdWindow.verbatim: Guest must exit the park before closing time (sunset) each day— no exceptions.

privacy.verbatim: Ceremony locations are public open spaces and there may be other ceremonies, members of the public, including children at, or near any ceremony location in Fort Williams Park.

fee: Effective January 1, 2025, the reservation fee is $400.00 (ceremony site reservation; guest parking fees are not included)
blocker: Ceremonies and photographs are not permitted on the Portland Head Light Parcel inside the park. (Town of Cape Elizabeth, Fort Williams Park Ceremony Regulations, as of Dec. 2024.) Separately: "All commercial photography at the lighthouse and in the park needs the approval of the Director of Fort Williams Park." Drones shall not operate within 300 feet of Portland Head Light.

name: Two Lights State Park headland
highlight: Forty-one acres of tilted, fractured granite dropping straight into open Atlantic, with picnic hills above the surf line. The twin 1828 towers that give the park its name stand outside it, at the end of Two Lights Road.

fact.verbatim: Special permits are not usually required for weddings, but some plans do require special permission. We urge you to plan your event carefully with the park manager to prevent surprises and disappointments on the big day.

permit.authority: Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands, Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry
permit.authorityContact: 207-799-5871 (Two Lights State Park); Bureau of Parks and Lands 207-287-3821

crowdWindow.verbatim: Open all year; 9:00 a.m. to sunset daily unless otherwise posted at the gate.

privacy.verbatim: Since parks are open to the public, privacy cannot be guaranteed, and wedding ceremonies tend to draw onlookers. Please consider this, especially where photography is concerned.

fee: Day-use fee at Two Lights: $5.00 Maine resident, $7.00 non-resident, $2.00 over-65 non-resident (per person, per day)
blocker: The general use of drones (UAS) is prohibited in Maine State Parks, Historic Sites, or DACF Boat Launches without direct oversight and guidance of an approved law enforcement agency or by the issue of a Special Activity Permit. The two lighthouses are outside the park boundary and are not publicly accessible — the western light is a private home.

name: Artists Bluff, Franconia Notch State Park
highlight: A short, steep scramble ends on open granite ledge directly above Echo Lake, looking south into the notch with Cannon's cliffs on the right and the Franconia Ridge on the left. The whole pass is visible from one rock.

fact.verbatim: Anyone wanting to plan an event at a State Park should contact that park directly and organize with the park manager to ensure the date and space is available, as well as to discuss pricing.  A Special Use Permit may also be required for events.

permit.authority: New Hampshire Division of Parks and Recreation, Department of Natural and Cultural Resources
permit.authorityContact: 603-271-3556 (Special Use Office); Franconia Notch State Park office 603-823-8800

crowdWindow.verbatim: Park initiatives include: increased staffing over peak foliage season to assist with visitor flow, traffic control, and on-site guidance; a one-way hiker traffic pattern on the Artists Bluff Trail to reduce congestion and improve hiker safety; enhanced signage and volunteer support to guide visitors during peak periods; and increased onsite facilities for food and beverage service, bathrooms, and trash disposal.

fee: All permits require submission of permit application and the administrative fee of $100. If the application is submitted less than 30 days prior to the event, an additional expedite fee of $100 will be required.
blocker: The tramway alternative to this viewpoint is out of service: "Please note: As of May 2026, the Cannon Mountain Aerial Tramway is closed and undergoing a replacement project. It is not expected to operate during the 2026 Summer season." Drone operators are not permitted to take off or land within NH State Park boundaries. Franconia Notch State Park sits inside the White Mountain National Forest — the surrounding forest is FEDERAL land under different rules.

name: Mount Washington State Park summit
highlight: A 58.8-acre patch of bare rock at 6,288 feet, the highest ground in the Northeast. On a clear day the view reaches the Atlantic; the weather changes inside of an hour.

fact.verbatim: Anyone wanting to plan an event at a State Park should contact that park directly and organize with the park manager to ensure the date and space is available, as well as to discuss pricing.  A Special Use Permit may also be required for events.

permit.authority: New Hampshire Division of Parks and Recreation, Department of Natural and Cultural Resources
permit.authorityContact: 603-466-3347 (Mt. Washington State Park); Special Use Office 603-271-3556

crowdWindow.verbatim:
June 13 – October 12
Gift Shop and Food Concessions: 8:30 am – 5:00 pm
​Lobby/Restrooms: 8:30 am - 6:00 pm

fee: All permits require submission of permit application and the administrative fee of $100. If the application is submitted less than 30 days prior to the event, an additional expedite fee of $100 will be required.
blocker: Published 2026 summit-building hours run May 22 – October 18. Access is by the privately operated Mount Washington Auto Road or Cog Railway, or on foot — the state park owns only the summit; the surrounding 800,000+ acres are White Mountain National Forest (FEDERAL). "The TIP TOP HOUSE is currently closed to the public for renovations. A re-opening date is not yet determined." Drone operators are not permitted to take off or land within NH State Park boundaries.
seasonalClosure: "During off hours and the off-season the park is typically not staffed, comfort stations are not available and gates may be closed. The off-season poses unique risks inherent when participating in outdoor recreational activities." — https://www.nhstateparks.org/find-parks-trails/mt-washington-state-park

name: Sterling Pond, Smugglers' Notch
highlight: A mile of steep trail from the height of the notch ends at Vermont's highest trout pond, held in a shallow bowl of spruce. Below, house-sized boulders sit in the road where they fell off the cliffs.

fact.verbatim: ANR lands are generally open to the public without fee or formal authorization for a wide variety of educational, recreational, and other outdoor activities for individuals or small groups.

permit.authority: Vermont Department of Forests, Parks and Recreation (Agency of Natural Resources) — Vermont State Parks

fee: No fee for ordinary small-group recreational use. If a special use permit is required: "Fees start at $50 per permit." Day use fees apply at the park.
blocker: A permit becomes required if "The activity is organized or publicized" or "The activity involves a fee charged to participants." Black bears are active daily at Smugglers' Notch State Park; food and aromatic items must be stowed.
seasonalClosure: Smugglers' Notch State Park Season: "Third weekend in May through the second Monday in October." — https://vtstateparks.com/smugglers.html (the VT-108 road through the notch is not maintained for through traffic in winter)

name: Quechee Gorge rim, Quechee State Park
highlight: Vermont's deepest gorge — the Ottauquechee runs 165 feet below the US-4 bridge between walls of grey schist. A short trail from the rim drops to the river at the bottom.

fact.verbatim: ANR lands are generally open to the public without fee or formal authorization for a wide variety of educational, recreational, and other outdoor activities for individuals or small groups.

permit.authority: Vermont Department of Forests, Parks and Recreation (Agency of Natural Resources) — Vermont State Parks

privacy.verbatim: The park's location along US Route 4, and its proximity to many upper-valley attractions make it a popular tourist destination. Hundreds of thousands of visitors stop each year to take in the breathtaking views of the Quechee Gorge.

fee: Day Use/Camping fees apply. If a special use permit is required: "Fees start at $50 per permit."
blocker: A permit becomes required if "The activity is organized or publicized" or "The activity involves a fee charged to participants." The state leases the park from the US Army Corps of Engineers — "In 1965, the State of Vermont leased the park from the Army Corps and turned over the management and operations of the property to the Department of Forests, Parks and Recreation."
seasonalClosure: Quechee State Park Season: "Memorial Day weekend through the second Monday in October." — https://vtstateparks.com/quechee.html

name: Boston Public Garden lagoon bridge
highlight: The first public botanical garden in America: Victorian bedding schemes, a lagoon with the Paget family's swan boats still running, and a small suspension bridge where the willows come down to the water.

fact.verbatim: No person shall, in any public park (including any boundary road thereof), or other public place (including any parkway) under the control of the Parks and Recreation Commission; unless under a lease or concession granted under Chapter 365 of the Acts of 1897, and unless a written permit be on their person or prominently displayed, engage in any commercial enterprise or solicit business or display or distribute any commercial advertising matter

permit.authority: City of Boston Parks and Recreation Department / Parks and Recreation Commission

crowdWindow.verbatim: enter, or remain in, any public park between the hours of 11:30 p.m. and 6:00 a.m. on any day except for the purpose of going through such park on the walks or malls thereof unless specific request is made for a particular facility, written to the Commissioner, and brought before the Commission and approved.

privacy.verbatim: Due to the wide variety of plants and its romantic setting, the Garden attracts many weddings.

blocker: Stay off the lawn and the beds. City rules prohibit any person from "sit, stand or lie upon lawn areas in the Public Garden except such lawn areas designated as sitting areas" and "go upon any flower bed or cultivated area"; the Public Grounds ordinance separately bars walking, standing or sitting on the grass in the Public Garden with no mayoral exemption available. Also barred: climbing on any "balustrade, railing, fence, wall, roof, statue, monument, fountain, bush or tree."

name: Walden Pond, Concord
highlight: A 102-foot-deep kettle pond left by a glacier, ringed by pine and oak, with the marked site of Thoreau's one-room house a short walk up from the water. Fog holds on it early before the lot fills.

fact.verbatim: You don’t need a separate permit to take photos and videos during a permitted wedding ceremony at a state park. If you don’t have a permit for your wedding, you need a special use permit to take photos and videos in a state park.

permit.authority: Massachusetts Department of Conservation and Recreation (DCR)

crowdWindow.verbatim: The parking lot will be closed once park reaches capacity. Closures are posted at mass.gov/parkalerts and on the outgoing message of the park phone: (978) 369-3254.

fee: Photography permit $45 per permit (DCR). Daily parking: $8 vehicles with MA plates, $30 vehicles registered out of state.
blocker: Walden Pond State Reservation in Concord does not allow any weddings from May 1 to Oct. 31, due to high recreational use during that time. (Massachusetts DCR, "Weddings at state parks.") Park restrictions also list "No drones." Park hours are 5:00 am–7:30 pm.

name: Mount Greylock summit
highlight: The highest ground in Massachusetts at 3,491 feet, with a lit granite war memorial tower on the bald summit and, on a clear day, about ninety miles of Taconic and Green Mountain ridgeline.

fact.verbatim: Interested in professional photography or a film/video production? The DCR maintains many facilities throughout the state that provides a perfect backdrop. You will need a permit.

permit.authority: Massachusetts Department of Conservation and Recreation (DCR)

crowdWindow.verbatim: Park is open dawn to dusk

fee: Photography permit $45 per permit (DCR). "Applications must be submitted with at least a 7 day notice" and a certificate of liability insurance naming DCR as additional insured with a minimum of $1,000,000 is required.
blocker: Summit restrictions include "No drones" and "No vehicles over 22 feet in length allowed on Mount Greylock Scenic Byway." "Veterans War Memorial Tower and Bascom Lodge open for the season May 23, 2026."
seasonalClosure: "Auto Roads to the summit open for the season May 16 through October 30, 2026" — https://www.mass.gov/locations/mount-greylock-state-reservation (outside that window the summit is reachable only on foot or by snowmobile)

name: Forty Steps, Newport Cliff Walk
highlight: Three and a half miles of public path wedged between Atlantic surf and the back lawns of the Gilded Age mansions. At Forty Steps a stone stair drops to a landing where the swell hits the rock directly underneath you.

permit.authority: City of Newport, Rhode Island (Cliff Walk Commission / Department of Public Services)
permit.authorityContact: 401-845-5300 (City of Newport, M-F 8:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m.) — https://www.cityofnewport.com/cliffwalk

blocker: Section closed: "Please be advised that as a result, the portion of the Cliff Walk between Narragansett Avenue and Webster Street will be closed for the foreseeable future. Visitors to the Cliff Walk are asked to follow detour signs and to not attempt to enter the restricted area." (City of Newport — the closed span is immediately south of Forty Steps.) The City publishes no permit rule covering photography or private gatherings on the Cliff Walk itself; its published park-reservation product is the King Park Gazebo, "reserved for small wedding ceremonies (not receptions), for a $100.00 (RESIDENT) or $250.00 (NON-RESIDENT) reservation fee." Call 401-845-5800 before assuming anything about the Cliff Walk.

name: Brenton Point State Park, Ocean Drive
highlight: Eighty-nine acres of open lawn on the last point of Aquidneck Island, where Narragansett Bay meets the Atlantic. Sixteen granite bollards of the Portuguese Discovery Monument stand in a semicircle facing the water.

fact.verbatim: Note: Photographers who are not charging for their services, do not need to become approved vendors for groups of 15 or less, as long as they remain in general use areas and do not infringe on the ability of other patrons to enjoy the park and recreate in general use areas.

permit.authority: Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management, Division of Parks and Recreation (RI State Parks)

privacy.verbatim:
Regardless of the time of year, you will need to contact the individual Park Office at 401-847-6740 or contact RI State Park Headquarters at 401-667-6200 or by emailing
DEM.RIparks@dem.ri.gov
if you intend to use the parks for an organized group gathering or event to determine if the activity requires a
Special Use Permit
.

fee: Commercial Photography Permit — Impact Cost: production size 1-25 = $25 cost per day per location. No fee for an unpaid photographer with a group of 15 or fewer in general use areas.
blocker: If you hire a paid photographer: "Professional photographers must be approved vendors if they are charging for their services, which constitutes “doing business” in state parks.  Any photo shoot that has more than 15 people, uses props, or in any way interferes with normal park activities will require a Special Use Permit in addition to becoming an approved vendor." Special Use Permit applications must be received online at least 30 days in advance.

name: Gillette Castle terrace, East Haddam
highlight: William Gillette's 1919 fieldstone house sits on the Seventh Sister hill, 200 feet above a bend in the Connecticut River. The outdoor terrace looks straight down the lower river valley.

fact.verbatim: Please note, the above information is for permitted weddings on the terrace, with use of the facility and assistance from park staff. As this is a state park, members of the public are allowed to hold small weddings on the grounds without getting a permit.

permit.authority: Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection (DEEP), State Parks Division

crowdWindow.verbatim: State parks and state forest recreation areas shall be open for public use daily between sunrise and sunset. Vehicles may enter daily from 8 a.m. and must leave the park by sunset.

privacy.verbatim: Those hosting events are reminded that the park is a public facility and visitors are permitted on the grounds until sunset.

fee: There is a non-refundable, non-transferable fee of $285 to rent the terrace for a wedding ceremony (terrace rental only; the grounds are free to use).
blocker: Do not apply through DEEP's Special Use process — "No weddings, private events, nor use of a drone by a member of the public are authorized through the Special Use application and process." Terrace rental, if you want it, is narrow: "The space is available to rent from June thru September, on Saturdays only" at 10:00 A.M. or 5:30 P.M. only, and "Weddings may be booked after January 31st for the upcoming season."

name: Herring Cove Beach
highlight: The one Outer Cape beach that faces west: the sun goes down into the water off the north lot, with the Provincetown skyline and Long Point behind you across the harbor.

fact.verbatim: A Special Use Permit (SUP) is required for activities that take place on park land or waters and provides a benefit to an individual, group or organization, rather than the public at large, and requires some degree of management from the National Park Service to protect park resources and the public interest.

permit.authority: Cape Cod National Seashore, National Park Service — FEDERAL, not Massachusetts DCR and not the Town of Provincetown

blocker: FEDERAL JURISDICTION FLAG: Herring Cove Beach, Race Point Beach, Coast Guard Beach, Nauset Light Beach and Marconi Beach are all inside Cape Cod National Seashore and are administered by the National Park Service — none of the five New England state-park regimes apply. NPS lists among the "Types of special events that generally require special use permits at the Cape Cod National Seashore": "Wedding ceremonies and informal receptions", "Filming" and "Still photography". Herring Cove is on the NPS list of "Locations generally available for special events." Route the permit question to Cape Cod National Seashore, not to mass.gov.
